OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from Western blots, ribosome profiling, and cycloheximide experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as the central finding with 'compelling evidence' and note that 'genetic evidence and ChIP data strongly support this claim.'

Both support microscopy findings on Hsf1 activity (C54-C57, C59-C62). OpenEval highlights concordance between Hsf1-GFP localization and gene coalescence assays. Peer reviewers praise 'innovative techniques including ribosome profiling and time-resolved localization' and treat these data as supporting evidence for Apj1's attenuation role.

Both strongly support ChIP evidence for Apj1 binding and Hsf1 displacement (C64-C72). OpenEval emphasizes temporal dynamics and inverse correlation with Hsf1 occupancy. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'genetic evidence and ChIP data strongly support this claim' regarding Apj1 displacing Hsf1 from promoters.

Both support comparative ChIP-qPCR data showing Apj1's preferential binding (C73-C76). OpenEval notes substantial quantitative differences (30-40-fold) and appropriate limitation of conclusions. Peer reviewers accept this as evidence for 'highly specific role for class A Apj1' that 'unveils specificity in the system.'

Both support double mutant data showing synergistic Hsf1 activation (C9, C40, C77, C80-C87, C89-C90, C115). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across translatome, Western blot, and microscopy data. Peer reviewers accept findings demonstrating distinct regulatory roles and praise the 'phased control model for Hsf1 by distinct JDPs.'

Both support genetic interaction and growth phenotype data (C91-C96). OpenEval highlights temperature-dependent phenotypes and epistasis with hsf1-848. Peer reviewers do not challenge these data and treat them as supporting the model of direct JDP control of Hsf1, noting the work 'raises additional new questions about JDP specificity.'

Both support J-domain mutant data showing requirement for Hsp70 interaction (C97-C98). OpenEval notes H34Q is well-established and demonstrates J-domain function is required. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the discovery that Apj1 regulates Hsf1 attenuation in a manner that includes Hsp70...is strongly supported by the experimental data.'

Both support microscopy data on Sis1-GFP foci and proteostasis defects (C99-C105). OpenEval argues these data support direct JDP regulation rather than protein damage as trigger. Peer reviewers accept the observations and note the interpretation challenge is 'clearly and appropriately dealt with in the manuscript text and in experiments.'

Both support Sis1 overexpression data showing dissociation between Hsf1 repression and growth rescue (C107-C109). OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates specificity of Apj1's role in Hsf1 regulation versus PQC functions. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting evidence for distinguishing direct effects on Hsf1 from indirect proteostasis effects.

Both evaluate phase-specific JDP functions (C110-C113, C128). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting experimental data support phase-specific functions but mechanistic explanation involving conformational states (C116) is speculative and model is incomplete. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, praising 'phased control model' as 'compelling and clear,' accepting some mechanistic details remain to be elucidated.

Both support translatome data on protein abundance (C119-C121). OpenEval notes consistency between prior literature and authors' measurements. Peer reviewers specifically appreciate 'innovative techniques including ribosome profiling' and note 'traditional gene expression assays added in revision...provide a compelling answer.'

Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 suggesting 'Perhaps Apj1...is the titrated Hsp70 (co)chaperone that determines the extent of the HSR?'

Both support Western blot data showing similar Hsf1 phosphorylation patterns (C63). OpenEval notes this negative result rules out alternative explanations. Peer reviewers do not challenge this control experiment, accepting it as consistent with the proposed mechanism of Apj1 acting through Hsp70-mediated displacement.
